Subject: Reserved capacity options — quick intake and next steps

Tom / Ellie,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, we want to map CadenceFord's anticipated inference footprint to a couple of concrete reserved-capacity options so procurement can evaluate budget and ramp risk. To keep things actionable, please send over a short weekly forecast (if you can) for the next 12 weeks — even a rough Calls/Hour and average tokens per call will help.

High-level info we need to propose concrete offers:
- Baseline concurrent throughput target (calls/sec or calls/min)
- Preferred hard minimum GPUs you need carved out at month 0 (if any)
- Peak/burst windows (days/times of week and expected multiplier)
- Any uncompromisable latency SLOs for p95 token latency

I can assemble two clean options: a low-commit pilot slate and a committed baseline with smoother ramp credits. Will include minimum GPU counts, recommended staging schedule, prewarm credits and a simple cost comparison. Can you share the forecast file by EOD Monday?

Attached: none yet — we’ll produce the proposal after your forecast.

Best,

Thanks, attached is a simple forecast (CadenceFord_Demand_Forecast.xlsx). We’ve sketched two scenarios internally:
1) Conservative pilot: start with 8 GPUs steady, assume growth to ~24 GPUs in 6–8 weeks if pilot metrics look good.

We’re leaning toward starting smaller, then ramping quickly if latency and cost look good. From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 14:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity options — quick intake and next steps

David —

Saw Tom’s forecast. Quick thoughts to shape the offer:
- Minimum carve: for a smooth pilot I’d recommend a 12-GPU reserved lane rather than 8. 8 GPUs risks queuing at peak and increases tail latency — which kills evaluations.
- Pilot ramp cadence: 12 -> 24 over 3 weeks (triggered by utilization thresholds) is a safer play; allow burst credits to 48 for known campaign windows.
- Committed profile: 24 min GPUs with contractual burst to 72, tiered discounts at 24 and 48 steady-state thresholds.
- Warmup/prewarm credits: include 200 prewarm GPU-hours to reduce cold-start variance during month 1.
- SLA/escape hatch: 30-day trial-eyes window (short) with a one-time decommit option in month 2 if utilization stays below 35% for full two-week window.

I’ll draft the two-option matrix (Pilot vs Committed) with price delta and activation triggers. Marissa — can you drop the cost deltas for quantized vs FP16 profiles for CadenceFord's token mix?

Karthik

--- Forwarded message ---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:36:12 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — Pilot vs Committed (summary)
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Summary (concise):
Option A — Pilot (low-commit):
- Baseline: 8 reserved GPUs for weeks 0–2; auto-scale to 16 if utilization > 65% for 48 hours; target ramp to 24 by week 6 if metrics clear.
- Burst: programmatic burst up to 48 GPUs (pay-as-you-go burst pricing).
- Credits: 150 GPU prewarm hours and 30% discount on batch quantized workloads during pilot.
- Pricing: lower fixed monthly, higher token unit for bursts.

Option B — Committed baseline (higher-commit, smoother economics):
- Baseline: 24 reserved GPUs starting month 0 with guaranteed throughput; contractual burst up to 72 GPUs.
- Ramp: staged add in months 1–3 to reach 48 steady-state if utilization triggers met.
- Credits: 400 GPU prewarm hours, 20% committed discount across model profiles.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime target; 2-week escape clause in first 60 days for usage mismatch.

Activation timeline (typical):
- Week 0: provisioning + prewarm (48–72 hours to stabilize caches).
- Weeks 1–3: pilot telemetry + trigger-based adds.
- Weeks 4–8: steady ramp or conversion to committed.

Attachments: redwood_reserve_offer_v2.pdf (proposal with pricing matrix)

Next step: pick Option A or B; we’ll prepare contract and a 1-page activation runbook. Decision requested by Sept 6 to meet provisioning windows for mid-September start.

Best,
David
